To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gene mph (C), which confers resistance to macrolid antibiotics on Staphlococcus aureus, encodes a phosphorotransferase and is expressed only when the msr(A )gene is present.
the msr(A)-mph(C) gene cluster on plasmid pHMS97 confers resistance to a wide range of macrolide antibiotics, including 14-, 15- and 16-member ring macrolides.
the mph(C) phosphotransferases is responsible for the inactivation of some macrolide compounds by the strain carrying plasmid pM597.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characteristic expression of msr(A),mph(C) and erm (Y) genes that confer resistance to erythromycins, and the inactivation mechanism of macrolides by the strain NCTC83252 containing pMS97.
the characterization of three genes, namely msr(A), erm(Y) and mph(C), that confer resistance on Staphylococeus aureus to macrolide-type antibiotics.
the characteristic expression of three genes that confer resistance to 14- and 15-membered macrolides on Staphyloccus aureus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

erythromycin resistance in the strain NCTC83255 containing plasmid MS97 is due to the action of both msr(A) (ABC-transporter-mediated resistance) and mph(C), which inactivates some erythromycin derivatives.
the msr(A)-mph(C) gene cluster confers erythromycin resistance on S. aureus.
msr(A), erm(Y) and mph(C), together or separately, confer resistance to macromolecules on S. aureus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the msr(A)-mph(C) gene cassette is responsible for the inactivation of macrolides by S. aureus.
the msr(A)-mph(C) genes on plasmid pHK3 confer resistance to macrotides on S. aureus by a novel mechanism.
the msr(A)-mph(C)-erm(Y) genes on plasmid MS97 encode a three-gene cluster that confers resistance to macrolid antibiotics.
